items.title: Meloni Blames Pro-Russia Hackers for Cyberattack on Minister
items.content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for a cyberattack on her foreign minister, after a rise in hybrid disruptions from entities aligned with Vladimir Putin’s government.

items.title: AI Safety Advocates Make Gains After $110 Million Midterm Fight
items.content: Candidates who favor stricter oversight of artificial intelligence racked up wins in key congressional races, aided by a pro-regulation political funding group backed in part by Anthropic PBC at a time when Americans are increasingly uneasy over the rapidly developing technology.

items.title: AI Trade Faces a Post-Election Reality Check
items.content: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Yorkville Ives & Co. partner Dan Ives and Bloomberg US equities reporter Natalia Kniazhevich examine the sharp post-election technology selloff, as investors weigh political resistance to data centers, AI spending and the outlook for Anthropic's IPO. They tell hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the election could slow the AI buildout and reshape winners and losers across tech, even as Ives argues the long-term AI investment cycle remains intact. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: AI Selloff Exposes Data Center Boom Risks
items.content: The selloff in AI stocks is adding new uncertainty to the massive buildout of data centers across the US. Jolienne Halisky, CFO of AIB Data Centers, says financing for new projects could become more expensive and take longer as lenders reassess risk, while permitting, power and chip availability remain constraints. She joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss her company's plans for its first Texas data center, concerns surrounding its anchor tenant Nebius, and why she believes the recent AI market rout will prove temporary. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Brookfield CEO Says Infrastructure Is Growing Fastest
items.content: Brookfield Asset Management raised $25 billion in the third quarter, driven by credit and infrastructure, as the money manager positions itself as a key player funding the build-out of artificial intelligence. He speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger.  (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Time to Move Forward With 'Sensible' AI Regulation, Says Rep. Liccardo
items.content: Democrat Representative from California Sam Liccardo said that congress has 'issued a lot of press releases' on issues surrounding technology, but haven't managed to push meaningful legislation over the finish line. Liccardo, whose district includes parts of Silicon Valley, said it is critical lawmakers act on AI concerns and that it is time to move forward with 'sensible' regulation.  (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Power On: How Private Is an Always-Listening Apple Watch?
items.content:
Apple is bringing some its most ambitious AI capabilities to its products. As AI becomes increasingly woven into daily life, questions over privacy are likely to follow.

On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov discuss privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Data Center Delays Risk an ‘Air Gap’ for Chips: Lovell
items.content: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says data center delays could create an “air gap” for semiconductors, pressuring inventories, prices and margins. She favors compute over memory and hyperscalers with existing capacity. She speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Tech Stocks Rebound as Dip Buyers Return to AI Trade
items.content: Bloomberg’s Tim Stenovec takes a look at what's driving a rebound in tech stocks as dip buyers step in to support the battered AI trade. Plus, Anthropic's IPO plans are hit by the post-election selloff, prompting prospective investors to rethink the company's expected valuation; and the CEOs of Lyft and DraftKings join to break down their earnings results. (Source: Bloomberg)
